notes.title: Canonical ordered Bregman formula
notes.plain: One canonical total real function Dψ(a,b)=ψ(a)-ψ(b)-Dψ(b)[a-b], using the actual Frechet derivative fderiv of ψ. The second argument is the base. At a nondifferentiable base fderiv defaults to zero; this total algebraic formula alone is not a source differentiability, positivity, metric or separation theorem. The core uses any real normed vector space; only the gradient conversion needs a complete real inner-product space. The source is finite Euclidean, ψ:X->R strictly convex/differentiable on intX; source-domain and ambient-extension locality are not silently identified.
notes.intuition: Subtract the affine approximation at the base from the function value at the target.
notes.why: Lower the required Chapter2 general prescient dependency frontier while preserving source residuals and nonsmooth losses.

notes.plain: One canonical total real function Dψ(a,b)=ψ(a)-ψ(b)-Dψ(b)[a-b], using the actual Frechet derivative fderiv of ψ. The second argument is the base. At a nondifferentiable base fderiv defaults to zero; this total algebraic formula alone is not a source differentiability, positivity, metric or separation theorem. notes.title: Nonsmooth proximal comparison retains both residuals
notes.plain: One canonical total real function Dψ(a,b)=ψ(a)-ψ(b)-Dψ(b)[a-b], using the actual Frechet derivative fderiv of ψ. The second argument is the base. At a nondifferentiable base fderiv defaults to zero; this total algebraic formula alone is not a source differentiability, positivity, metric or separation theorem. The core uses any real normed vector space; only the gradient conversion needs a complete real inner-product space. The source is finite Euclidean, ψ:X->R strictly convex/differentiable on intX; source-domain and ambient-extension locality are not silently identified. The supplied p belongs to V and actually minimizes f(z)+ηinverse Dψ(z,x) there; f is real convex on the same V, η>0, and ψ is ambient differentiable at BOTH x and p. x may be outside V. No loss derivative, ψ convexity/strictness, closedness, coercivity or existence theorem is required by this real helper. It concludes the comparison for every u in V with both negative residuals retained. Nonnegative residual values require separate convexity hypotheses; they cannot be discarded from this theorem alone.
notes.intuition: Use the actual proximal minimum, differentiating the regularizer rather than the nonsmooth loss.
notes.why: Lower the required Chapter2 general prescient dependency frontier while preserving source residuals and nonsmooth losses.
notes.position: Orabona, Online Learning, arXiv:1912.13213v10 (2026-06-21), Chapter2 printed14/PDF26 forward observation; Definition6.4 printed63/PDF75, nonnegativity and Lemma6.7 printed64/PDF76; Section15.5.1 Algorithm15.8/Theorem15.30 printed265–266/PDF277–278. PDF SHA256 cef4edfa97a6e063e53e9c532717c50aa156e5bc782ea49f969b3385011a1b17. Theorem15.30 proof-step dependency; not the complete performance theorem.
notes.proof_idea: Differentiate only h(z)=ηinverse Dψ(z,x) at the selected minimum p. Its derivative is ηinverse(Dψ(p)-Dψ(x)). The accepted real nonsmooth convex-minimizer comparison gives f(p)-f(u)<=ηinverse(Dψ(p)-Dψ(x))[u-p]. Multiply by positive η and use the three-point identity with (p,x,u), obtaining Dψ(u,x)-Dψ(u,p)-Dψ(p,x). The previous-base derivative hypothesis is retained for source validity even though the fixed dual map is already linear in this proof. This is an actual-minimum comparison, not an assumed regret/stability bound or a sequence construction.
